title: Surprise protests, GenZ outreach: Rahul Gandhi's new playbook after CJP's success
content: Rahul Gandhi’s political style has taken a more combative turn, with the Congress leader increasingly combining Gen Z outreach, parliamentary interventions and surprise street protests. From Bharat Jodo and Chhatron Ki Goonj to student protests and dharnas, the story looks at how Rahul is trying to stay with issues longer, while also navigating criticism.

title: After handcuff footage, ECB takes big call on Carse before Pakistan 2nd Test
content: England drop Brydon Carse from the second Test against Pakistan after footage shows the fast bowler in handcuffs outside a Derby nightclub. The Cricket Regulator is investigating the incident. Carse was reportedly released without charge after celebrating Durham’s County Championship win. The episode adds to recent disciplinary concerns involving England players following other nightclub-related incidents.

title: Mark Zuckerberg’s wife Priscilla Chan’s $125 million school to shut after 10 years
content: After a decade of service, The Primary School, a free private institution, has officially closed its doors. This decision follows the conclusion of financial backing from the Chan Zuckerberg Initiative and the school's inability to meet state academic standards. As a result, approximately 540 students are set to transfer to the Ravenswood City Elementary School District, with the Chan Zuckerberg Initiative facilitating their transition and savings.

title: Mamdani’s team sends memo to ‘upset’ New Yorkers over million-dollar home tax
content: In a recent development, New York City's Finance Commissioner delivered a memo about the pied-à-terre tax that he could not present in person due to ongoing litigation. The memo specifies that the supplemental roll does not automatically create tax liabilities for property owners. To evade the surcharge, homeowners are encouraged to provide evidence of their primary residency. Notably, the deadline for lodging appeals has been broadened until September 18, 2026.

title: Maine's Sand Beach was once part of J.P. Morgan's 117-acre wedding gift
content: A stretch of Maine coastline that was once part of a wealthy family’s private summer estate is now open to visitors as part of Acadia National Park. The land was donated in 1949 by Eleanor Morgan Satterlee in memory of her mother, Louisa, after the family property was badly damaged in the 1947 fire.

title: Alabama students turn old Christmas trees into Gulf Coast dune protection
content: Alabama's fragile sand dunes are being restored with discarded holiday trees, as students and volunteers team up to plant native vegetation along the coast. This innovative project marries sand trapping techniques with the introduction of native plants to stabilize the dunes. This effort not only protects essential infrastructure but also fosters crucial habitats for local wildlife, showcasing an eco-friendly method for coastal restoration and habitat recovery.

title: Perplexity, which wanted to buy Chrome, in talks with Nvidia for money
content: Perplexity, the AI search startup led by Aravind Srinivas that once made an unsolicited $34.5 billion bid for Google's Chrome browser, is now in talks with Nvidia for funding. The Information reports the round would value Perplexity above $30 billion, up more than 50 percent from its last valuation, as annualised revenue climbs past $750 million on the back of its Perplexity Computer agent.

title: McGregor reacts to Stone Cold meme with four words after UFC 329 exit
content: Conor McGregor joked that a Stone Cold Steve Austin and Vince McMahon meme matched his August. The reaction came after his UFC 329 injury and recovery. Meanwhile, Khabib Nurmagomedov described McGregor as his toughest mental challenge at that stage of his career, while making clear that Justin Gaethje later presented a harder overall fight for him inside the Octagon there.

title: Did Simon Nemec request a trade from Devils before Flames move?
content: Before becoming a member of the Calgary Flames, Simon Nemec has clarified that he did not ask for a trade from the New Jersey Devils. 22-year-old defenseman said the change of management in New Jersey and his fit in the organization were factors in the move. Nemec has since seized the opportunity in Calgary, signing to a five-year deal and expecting to play a larger role on the blue line.

title: Who is Avery Styles? Meet AJ Styles' son making his wrestling debut
content: Avery Styles, son of wrestling legend AJ Styles, has begun his professional wrestling career. He made his debut in June 2026 and quickly gained significant attention. Styles then signed a contract with TNA, a major wrestling promotion. This signing occurred after his appearance at the Lockdown event. Avery Styles is now forging his own path in the wrestling world.

title: Trump's 'Op Economic Outcast' against Iran: What sanctions threat could mean for India
content: The Donald Trump administration said on Monday that the new US sanctions are intended to shut off every potential source of revenue for Iran, while warning other countries that continuing their economic ties with Tehran could expose them to retaliation.

title: The Oval Obese: Trump's junk food habit crashes into MAHA crusade
content: President Trump's administration champions the importance of healthy eating and providing nutritious options to Americans. However, his fondness for fast food and sugary beverages presents a notable contradiction. This discrepancy weakens the central theme of the 'Make America Healthy Again' initiative. Health professionals emphasize that the president's weight warrants greater concern than his wardrobe, creating a dilemma for the administration in promoting healthy lifestyle choices effectively.

title: Pant breaks another record in Colombo, surpasses Gilchrist in six-hitting feat
content: In a phenomenal display of skill, Rishabh Pant has outshone Adam Gilchrist's Test six record, achieving an impressive 102 sixes over just 52 matches, positioning him third globally. Additionally, he has set a new benchmark as India's highest run-scorer among wicketkeepers in away Tests, surpassing MS Dhoni's previous record. Furthermore, Pant leads India in the World Test Championship run-scorer tally.

title: Costa Rica spread 12,000 tonnes of orange waste; forest biomass later rose 176%
content: In 1998, about 12,000 metric tonnes of orange peels and pulp were spread over a degraded pasture in Costa Rica as part of an unusual forest restoration experiment. Sixteen years later, researchers found that the site had developed into a dense forest, with richer soil, greater tree diversity and a 176% increase in aboveground biomass.

title: Himanshi Khurana claims she has proof in Asim Riaz ‘conversion’ row
content: Himanshi Khurana has hit back at Asim Riaz's outright rejection of her claims, expressing her willingness to present evidence such as CCTV footage and audio recordings. She also brought to light the violence she endured during their relationship, underlining the importance of keeping her discussions respectful despite their personal nature. Khurana reiterated her right to share her experiences and lessons learned openly.

title: Nagpur chlorine leak horror: 56 hospitalised, 8 fighting for life in ICU
content: A chlorine gas leak at a Nagpur water treatment plant sent 56 residents to hospital. Eight patients remain in the ICU while 11 have been discharged. Emergency responders submerged the faulty chlorine tank to contain the dangerous gas. Health teams are conducting door-to-door checks for delayed symptoms. An inquiry is underway to determine the exact cause of the leakage.

title: US unleashes ‘Malice’: F-35C gets a 463-km air-to-air strike reach
content: The US Navy has introduced the AIM-424 missile, specifically engineered for the F-35C fighter jet. With a remarkable range exceeding 463 kilometers for air-to-air combat, this advanced missile maintains the aircraft's stealth attributes by allowing for internal carriage. The AIM-424 significantly boosts the F-35C's operational capabilities, while adversaries like Russia and China are rapidly advancing their own long-range missile programs.

title: Allahabad HC rejects Atiq Ahmed's eldest son Mohammad Umar's bail plea
content: The Allahabad High Court denied bail to Mohammad Umar, the eldest son of Atiq Ahmed, who is under serious allegations of extortion and threats stemming from a case filed in the previous year. Presently, he remains incarcerated in Lucknow jail. Meanwhile, his sibling Ali has been granted temporary parole for a burial, as the Atiq Ahmed family grapples with devastating losses since 2023.

title: India's 2026 Hockey WC semi-final race ends with 3-5 loss to Argentina
content: India’s men’s hockey team exit the 2026 World Cup semi-final race after losing 3-5 to Argentina. Two early goals put India on the back foot, while poor passing and missed penalty corners hurt their comeback hopes. Sukhjeet scores twice and Hardik adds a penalty stroke, but Argentina’s five-goal haul seals victory. India now play for seventh or eighth place.

title: From property registration to parking: What Karnataka’s 8 new Bills mean for you
content: Karnataka has passed eight new Bills that significantly influence property registration and land management in the state. These regulations will implement remote e-registration and bolster digital frameworks for property dealings. Unapproved rural properties must now comply with town planning guidelines. Additionally, park land can be designated for public utilities under strict oversight, while other Bills focus on refining commercial regulations and enhancing Bengaluru's transport system.

title: Hits on government sites during Operation Sindoor: NIA begins probe
content:
NIA searches five states in cyberterror case over attempted DDoS attacks on govt websites during Operation Sindoor

NEW DELHI: NIA conducted searches at five locations in Maharashtra, Gujarat, Telangana, Bihar and Delhi Monday in connection with attempted distributed denial of service attacks against govt websites during Operation Sindoor. The accused in the Gujarat cyber terrorism case - registered on June 25, 2025 - had attempted sophisticated DDoS attacks against 54 websites of govt entities, targeting critical computer resources and CII . Two accused have already been arrested. During probe, suspects who had provided support and assistance to the accused were identified through technical analysis. Searches were conducted and digital devices and documents containing incriminating material related to hacking activities were seized. The suspects were examined regarding their association with the accused in custody.

End of Article
